title: Glossary
description: A collection of technical terms and their definitions

terms.definition: The low-level contract (calling conventions, data layout) between compiled components or between a guest and the hypervisor.
An ordered list of rules granting or denying access to a resource.
The protocol certbot speaks to a certificate authority to prove domain control and obtain or renew certificates automatically.
Open standard for hardware discovery, configuration, and power management exposed by firmware to the OS.
Copyleft licence requiring source disclosure even when the software is offered only over a network; used by Xen Orchestra.
Nutanix's KVM-based hypervisor; one of the platforms VMware migrants come from.
RISC CPU architecture family; a Xen porting target alongside x86 and RISC-V.
The 64-bit Arm instruction set; a Xen/XCP-ng porting target.
7-bit character encoding for basic Latin text.
terms.abbreviation: American Standard Code for Information Interchange

terms.definition: A tag on TLB entries letting the CPU distinguish address spaces without full TLB flushes; relevant to Xen context-switch performance.
The read-only parent image left in a VDI chain after a snapshot; reaped by garbage collection once the chain coalesces.
The combined practice of backing up data and being able to recover service after a disaster.
The routing protocol that exchanges reachability between autonomous systems; underpins EVPN/overlay fabrics.
Low-level firmware that initialises server hardware before the OS boots; its power and Turbo settings can affect VM performance.
A XAPI object flag listing operations forbidden on a VM; XOA sets it so the appliance cannot accidentally destroy itself. Cleared with xe vm-param-remove.

Dedicated chip on the server motherboard that lets you power-cycle, access the BIOS, and monitor hardware health out-of-band — even when the OS is off or crashed. iDRAC (Dell), iLO (HPE), and XCC (Lenovo) are BMC implementations; IPMI is the open standard protocol that BMCs speak.
Several NICs combined into one logical network link for redundancy or higher throughput.
A family of Unix-derived operating systems and the permissive licence sharing the name.
Modern Linux copy-on-write filesystem with built-in multi-disk RAID-like features. Used by Synology DSM on multi-bay NAS units; not native to XCP-ng but can appear in P2V / data-recovery scenarios.

Enhanced halt state that drops CPU voltage and frequency when a core is idle to save power. A BIOS-level setting that can add wake latency for latency-sensitive workloads; covered in Tobias Kreidl's tuning series.
An XO backup mode that keeps a near-live copy of a VM on another SR or pool by replicating incremental changes on a schedule.
Mechanism that records which blocks of a virtual disk have changed since the last snapshot, so subsequent backups only copy what's new instead of scanning the whole disk.
Kubernetes control-plane component that integrates the cluster with a cloud provider's APIs (load balancers, nodes, routes).
The standard EFF command-line client that requests and renews free Let's Encrypt (ACME) TLS certificates.
RRDtool's default way of condensing many raw samples into one stored data point by averaging them (others are MIN/MAX/LAST). Determines what XO's per-VM stats return at each granularity.

The standard tool that performs early initialization of a cloud VM on first boot — users, SSH keys, hostname, growing the root disk. XO can inject a cloud-init config when creating a VM from a template.
An open-source cloud-orchestration platform that can manage XCP-ng hosts as a hypervisor backend.
Software for authoring and publishing web content (e.g. Ghost, WordPress).
The background process that merges a chain of incremental disk snapshots back into the base disk after backups or snapshots. It is random-I/O heavy and can dominate disk load on slow storage.
empty
Relative share of CPU time a VM gets when hosts are contended; XO exposes it as Default/Quarter/Half/etc.
The x86 instruction (and the feature data it returns) by which software and the hypervisor discover CPU capabilities.
An XO backup mode that continuously replicates VM state to a remote target.
Standard API for exposing storage systems to container orchestrators such as Kubernetes; referenced here as a storage driver.
A request bundle, containing a public key and identity, submitted to a CA to obtain a certificate.
NVIDIA's parallel-computing platform and API for general-purpose GPU workloads.
An open-source 64-bit RISC-V application-class CPU core whose RTL is published; commonly run on FPGA. An example of open hardware at the core-design level (distinct from the open RISC-V ISA).
The standard identifier scheme for publicly disclosed security vulnerabilities.

CPU power-management scheme that scales frequency to load. The BIOS chooses who controls it: OS DBPM lets the hypervisor/OS govern P-states, System DBPM keeps control in firmware. A central topic of Tobias Kreidl's "Tale of Two Servers" Part 1.
The Linux distribution commonly used as the base OS when installing Xen Orchestra from sources (rather than using the XOA appliance).
A backup that stores only the blocks changed since the last full backup, reducing time and storage.
Protocol that automatically assigns IP addresses and network settings to hosts.
Hardware feature letting devices read/write memory without the CPU; the reason an IOMMU is needed for safe passthrough.
The distributed system that resolves names to IP addresses.
The first VM created by Xen, to run the management toolstack
A regular VM running under the control of Dom0
Libraries for fast user-space packet processing that bypass the kernel network stack.
Keeping a replicated copy offsite so workloads can be brought up if the primary site is lost.
A distributed replicated storage system for the Linux platform
The Linux kernel subsystem managing GPUs and display (KMS); relevant to guest graphics and passthrough.
Documented procedures for restoring IT services after a major outage or disaster.
VMware's feature that load-balances VMs across hosts; a capability often compared against XCP-ng.
Text description of non-discoverable hardware for Arm/RISC-V boot; consumed by Xen and the kernel.
An ACME extension where the CA issues a key ID and HMAC secret so automated certificate requests are tied to a specific (often paid) account; required by CAs such as InCommon.
Security software that monitors a machine for threats; in XCP-ng the guidance is to run it inside VMs, not on the hypervisor host.
Firmware interface between platform firmware and the OS; see UEFI, its modern form.
The point after which a product or version no longer receives updates or support.
The RISC-V accelerator developed under the European Processor Initiative (EPI).
Community repository of add-on packages for RHEL and derivatives.
EU-funded programme to build sovereign European HPC processors; its main CPU line is Arm-based, with a RISC-V accelerator track (EPAC).
Intel's hardware-assisted nested paging for VMs (AMD's equivalent is NPT).
VMware's bare-metal hypervisor; the main platform XCP-ng migrants leave.
European standards body for ICT, including telecom and security standards.
Delivery of desktops and applications to end users (e.g. VDI); a workload class for virtualization platforms.
BGP-based control plane for Layer-2/3 VPNs over IP fabrics, commonly paired with VXLAN.
An alternative local SR type in XCP-ng that uses thin provisioning, meaning disk space is only consumed as data is written.
The process of bringing a replicated VM copy into service (after source loss, or as a migration cutover); for Continuous Replication targets it is the supported way to start the replica.
Open authentication standard (WebAuthn + CTAP) for passwordless and hardware-key login.
US government standards, notably FIPS 140 for validated cryptographic modules.
PCIe mechanism to reset an individual device function; important for clean device passthrough.
Software distributed under licences granting use, study, modification, and redistribution.
A reconfigurable logic chip programmed after manufacture.
XCP-ng background process that reclaims storage used by orphaned snapshot chains after backup or replication jobs.
Red Hat's shared-disk cluster filesystem allowing concurrent access from multiple nodes.
GitHub's built-in CI/CD automation system.
Amazon's low-cost archival storage tier; data retrieval takes hours. Dramatically cheaper than standard S3 but not suitable for frequent access.
Open implementation of OpenPGP for signing and encryption; used for package and release signing.
The copyleft licence requiring derivative works to remain under the same terms.
Specialised processor; in virtualisation it can be passed through or shared to VMs, with scheduler modes trading fairness against throughput.
A tunnelling protocol that wraps arbitrary network-layer packets inside IP.
The common Linux bootloader that loads the kernel (and the Xen hypervisor).
A card connecting a host to storage/network fabric (e.g. Fibre Channel, SAS).
Architecture combining compute and software-defined storage on the same nodes.
The list of hardware validated to work with a platform.
The maximum memory the Node.js xo-server process will allocate; independent of the VM's total RAM until configured.
Use of clustered, high-throughput compute for demanding workloads such as simulation and large-scale data processing.
Tamper-resistant device that generates and guards cryptographic keys.
HVM refers to a set of extensions that make it much simpler to virtualize the processor
The layer that runs virtual machines; in XCP-ng this is Xen plus the Dom0 control domain.
Systems and policies governing who can authenticate and what they may do.
Dell's brand name for its BMC — the out-of-band management card built into Dell PowerEdge servers. Lets you access the console and manage hardware without an OS.
Standards body for electrical and electronic technologies (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001).
Professional body and standards organisation (e.g. IEEE 802 networking).
terms.abbreviation: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

terms.definition: RISC-V interrupt controller delivering message-signalled interrupts; needed for dom0 console and IRQ handling on RISC-V.
A US research-and-education identity federation and certificate authority widely used by universities; issues certificates via ACME with EAB credentials.
Relative disk-IO scheduling weight given to a VM's storage traffic (sched-pri).
Hardware that translates and isolates device DMA addresses; the basis for safe PCI passthrough.
Linux command-line tool that reports CPU and per-device disk I/O statistics; used to spot storage bottlenecks on a host.
Virtualization of device I/O, most often via SR-IOV virtual functions.
A command-line tool that measures raw network throughput between two hosts, commonly used to rule the network in or out when diagnosing slow transfers.
Open standard (PICMG) for out-of-band server management. Defines the protocol that BMCs speak. ipmitool is the common CLI client.
Long-standing text chat protocol used by many open-source communities.

The contract between hardware and software defining a processor's instructions. RISC-V and POWER are *open* ISAs (royalty-free specifications); x86 and ARM are proprietary/licensed. An open ISA does not by itself make a chip open hardware or open firmware.
International standards body; also the common name for an optical-disc image file.
A special XCP-ng SR type that holds ISO files (CD/DVD images) for mounting as virtual optical drives in VMs. Backed by NFS, SMB, or local filesystem.
A company that builds and sells software, often as an ecosystem partner.
Runtime that executes Java bytecode.
A compact, signed token format used to carry claims for authentication/authorization.
A key used to encrypt other keys; in UEFI Secure Boot, the key authorising updates to the signature database.
In XO incremental backup chains, a KEY is a full backup taken at a set interval; all incrementals between two KEYs depend on each other.
The Linux in-kernel hypervisor; the basis of many competing virtualization stacks.
Protocol that bundles multiple links into one logical bonded interface.
A network confined to a single site or building.
Industry-standard directory protocol used for centralised authentication. XO has a plugin to authenticate users against LDAP/Active Directory.
A weaker-copyleft GPL variant allowing linking from non-GPL software.
Management layer from LINBIT that sits above DRBD. Handles provisioning, snapshots, and placement of replicated storage volumes across a cluster. The control plane for XOSTOR.
The primary mailing list where Linux kernel development happens.
Standard Linux command that lists the PCI devices physically present on a host, regardless of what XAPI has recorded. Useful for spotting "ghost" or stale device entries.
An XO backup setting that keeps the first backup of each day/week/month/year, so weekly/monthly fulls are retained without separate jobs.
A release line that receives fixes and support for an extended period.
A number used to identify a logical unit
A Python helper module in XCP-ng's storage manager (SMAPIv1) for LVHD (LVM-backed VHD) volume operations; imported by CloudStack's XCP-ng plugin.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_Volume_Manager_(Linux)
An XCP-ng storage-repository type that stores VM disks as LVM logical volumes.
OS-level virtualization using Linux namespaces and cgroups.
The hardware address identifying a network interface on a LAN.
The legacy disk partitioning and boot scheme preceding GPT/UEFI.
A hidden, high-privilege microcontroller in Intel platforms running closed firmware; a central concern for hardware self-sovereignty and auditability. AMD's counterpart is the PSP.
A Broadcom/LSI tri-mode hardware RAID controller (16 internal ports), driven by mpi3mr.
Authentication requiring two or more independent factors.
Device registers exposed in the CPU's address space so I/O looks like memory access.
Linux kernel driver for Broadcom's newer tri-mode (SAS/SATA/NVMe) storage controllers (MegaRAID 9500 / Aero family); hardware support depends on the driver knowing the card's PCI ID.
Carrier networking technique that forwards packets by short labels rather than IP lookups.
Lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol common in IoT.
PCIe interrupt delivery via memory writes rather than dedicated pins; handled by the hypervisor for guests.
A company that operates IT services on behalf of customers; a key XCP-ng/XO channel.
Microsoft's relational database; a common Windows VM workload.
The largest packet size a network link will carry; mismatches cause fragmentation or drops.
File-level storage served over the network (e.g. NFS/SMB).
Rewriting of IP addresses/ports as traffic crosses a boundary.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_block_device
Standard protocol (originally Sun/RFC 1813) for sharing directories over a network so remote machines can mount them as local filesystems. One of the supported SR types in XCP-ng.
A physical network port on a server. A bond combines several NICs into one logical link.
Tag added to a VDI name (e.g. mydisk [NOSNAP]) to tell backup and migration operations to skip the snapshot step for that disk. Useful when the source SR is too full to hold a snapshot.
VMware's network virtualization/SDN product.
Microsoft Windows' native filesystem. Reading or writing it on a Linux host (such as XCP-ng dom0) needs the ntfs-3g driver, which is not installable from dom0's default repos.
Keeps server clocks synchronised over a network; clock drift between hosts can cause subtle storage, backup, and authentication failures.
Intel's small-form-factor mini-PC line, popular for homelabs.
On multi-socket servers, memory attached to one CPU socket is faster for that socket; keeping a VM's CPUs and memory in the same NUMA node improves performance.
A fast storage interface protocol used by modern SSDs, operating over PCIe. Can be passed through directly to a VM for near-bare-metal storage performance.
openSUSE build system for compiling and signing packages across distributions; considered here as a signing backend.
Standards body defining container image and runtime formats.
A company whose hardware is sold or rebranded by another vendor; a hardware-partner channel.
Identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 for federated single sign-on.
An open-source SDN controller.
The condition where a system exhausts available RAM; the Linux kernel's OOM killer then terminates processes to recover memory.
Policy engine that evaluates declarative authorization/admission rules, e.g. at a gateway.
The firmware runtime-services interface on bare-metal OpenPOWER systems (implemented by the skiboot firmware); the PowerNV equivalent of what PAPR/RTAS provide to virtualized POWER guests.
Open hardware/firmware initiative built around the POWER instruction set, enabling fully open bare-metal POWER systems (e.g. Raptor's Talos/Blackbird).
The open-source RISC-V firmware implementing the SBI runtime-services contract between the OS (supervisor mode) and machine mode; a genuinely open firmware layer on RISC-V.
Open-source silicon root-of-trust project (secure boot and hardware identity); a rare example of open-hardware security silicon.
The seven-layer reference model for networking; also the Open Source Initiative in licensing contexts.
Software released under a licence permitting use, modification, and redistribution.
A single-use code, often time-based (TOTP), used as a second authentication factor.
A single-file (tar) packaging of an OVF virtual machine for distribution.
Open-source UEFI firmware (built from EDK II) used to boot virtual machines; packaged here for XCP-ng.
SDN layer on top of Open vSwitch providing virtual networks, considered as a networking option.
The software-defined virtual switch used by XCP-ng to manage VM network traffic.
The management protocol/schema for configuring Open vSwitch.
Nonprofit producing widely-used web application security guidance (e.g. the OWASP Top 10).
Xen memory mapping from guest-physical to machine (host) addresses; implemented in xen/arch/x86/mm/p2m*.c.
Process of converting a physical machine into a VM, typically by imaging its disks and rebuilding the boot chain inside the hypervisor.
The specification for how a POWER guest talks to a hypervisor (hypercalls + RTAS); the interface the pSeries platform implements.
/storage/#-how-to-modify-an-existing-sr-connection
Proxmox's deduplicating backup server; appears in competitive comparisons with Xen Orchestra backup.
The bus standard (PCIe) for attaching devices; the unit of device passthrough. (In payments, PCI also = PCI DSS.)
The vendor:device identifier a Linux driver matches against to claim a device; a missing ID means the driver won't bind and the hardware appears absent.
A technique that lets a VM access a physical hardware device (GPU, NVMe, etc.) directly, bypassing the hypervisor's virtualization layer for near-native performance.
The index of a physical memory page; central to Xen's memory mapping.
IBM's proprietary firmware hypervisor (the core of PowerVM) that runs beneath pSeries guests.
/project/architecture/#pifs
Smart-card standard (FIPS 201) for credential-based authentication.
A family of cryptography standards (e.g. PKCS#11 for HSM interfaces).
The RISC-V external interrupt controller; part of the Xen-on-RISC-V bring-up.
A small build demonstrating feasibility before fuller investment.
A group of XCP-ng hosts that share configuration, storage, and a single XAPI database. Operations like VM migration and shared SRs are scoped to a pool.
The bare-metal OpenPOWER platform type, where the OS runs directly on the hardware via OPAL firmware with no hypervisor beneath. Contrast pSeries.
IBM's proprietary virtualization stack for POWER (the PHYP hypervisor plus tooling); runs pSeries guests.
Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attacks by quantum computers.
A network setting that lets a virtual interface receive all traffic on its segment, not just frames addressed to it.
The POWER platform type for running as a guest under a hypervisor (PowerVM/KVM) via the PAPR interface. Contrast PowerNV (bare metal).
AMD's on-die security coprocessor running closed, high-privilege firmware; the AMD counterpart to Intel's Management Engine (ME), and a hardware self-sovereignty concern.
https://wiki.xenproject.org/wiki/Paravirtualization_(PV)
A lightweight Xen guest mode: hardware virtualization for CPU/memory with paravirtualized I/O and no emulated devices.
An HVM guest that loads paravirtual (PV) drivers for fast disk/network I/O.
Standard for booting a machine from the network.
QEMU's modern PCIe-based emulated chipset for VMs (vs the legacy i440FX).
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qcow
A disk image format used by XCP-ng that supports thin provisioning and snapshots more efficiently than the older VHD format.
Open-source machine emulator/virtualizer; provides device emulation for HVM guests under Xen.
Combining disks for redundancy and/or performance.

A disk-array layout that survives two simultaneous drive failures by storing double parity. The trade-off is a heavier write penalty than mirroring (RAID-1/10), which matters for write-heavy workloads such as backups.
Authorization model granting permissions to roles, which are assigned to users.
An architectural style for HTTP APIs using resources and standard verbs.
Xen Orchestra's HTTP interface under /rest/v0/… for scripting against XO (list VMs, read stats, import/patch, etc.).
A server (nginx, Caddy, HAProxy, etc.) placed in front of an application that terminates TLS and forwards plain traffic to the application behind it.
The IETF document series defining internet standards and protocols.
Red Hat's commercial Linux distribution; a common guest OS.
CPU design philosophy with simple, regular instructions; the basis of RISC-V.
Invoking a procedure in another address space or host as if local.
The package format and tool used by RHEL/CentOS and XCP-ng's dom0.
The maximum acceptable data loss, measured as the age of the last usable backup.
XCP-ng/XAPI procedure that patches a pool host-by-host, evacuating VMs to avoid downtime.
A fixed-size time-series store (rrdtool); XAPI records host and VM performance metrics as RRDs.
A widely-used public-key cryptosystem.
Firmware-provided runtime services on POWER (reboot, error logging, device config) that a pSeries guest calls; part of the PAPR contract.
The hardware-design abstraction (in Verilog/VHDL) describing a chip's logic. An "open RTL" core publishes this source (e.g. CVA6) — open hardware at the design level, distinct from an open ISA.
Object storage protocol popularized by AWS; XO supports any S3-compatible provider for backup remotes.
Enterprise drive interface, higher reliability and throughput than SATA but slower than NVMe; common in rack servers.
UEFI Secure Boot revocation mechanism using component generation numbers (sbat.csv) instead of revoking individual binaries.
A formal inventory of the components and dependencies in a piece of software.
Decoupling network control from forwarding so networks are programmable.
Storage pooled and managed in software across commodity nodes; XOSTOR is XCP-ng's software-defined storage.
In CloudStack, the storage for templates, snapshots and ISOs (as opposed to primary storage for running VM disks).
AMD feature encrypting a VM's memory to isolate it from the hypervisor; of interest to Xen confidential computing.
File transfer over an SSH-secured channel.
A family of cryptographic hash functions (SHA-1/2/3).
Platform that aggregates and correlates security logs for detection and response.
A distinct sellable product/variant identifier.
A contract defining the service quality (e.g. uptime, response times) a provider commits to.
IPv6 mechanism by which hosts self-assign addresses from router advertisements.
https://github.com/xapi-project/xapi-storage
The first-generation XCP-ng storage data path (tapdisk-based); the older, slower route newer storage work aims to move past.
Microsoft file-sharing protocol (also called CIFS). One of the supported share types for ISO SRs in XCP-ng.
Log file for SMAPI activity at /var/log/SMlog; on busy pools this is typically the dominant /var/log consumer.
Multiple CPUs/cores sharing memory under one OS; vCPU scheduling concerns the hypervisor.
Protocol for monitoring and managing network devices.
AMD SEV-SNP feature adding memory-integrity protection for confidential VMs; relevant to Xen guest support.
The team/function that monitors and responds to security events.
User-space libraries for high-performance, polled-mode storage I/O.
The standard language for relational databases.
/storage
An RPM package containing source code and the spec to build binary RPMs.
Plural of SRPM; the source packages directory/set for a distribution.
Flash-based storage device with no moving parts.
The legacy name (now TLS) for the protocol securing network connections.
The encryption layer behind https:// connections; TLS is the modern successor to the older SSL.
terms.abbreviation: Secure Sockets Layer / Transport Layer Security

terms.definition: Authenticating once to gain access to multiple applications.
Linux service that connects hosts to central identity providers (LDAP/AD/Kerberos).
XAPI's pool database file — the single source of truth for which VMs, hosts and storage exist in the pool.
US DoD hardening guides for configuring systems securely.
A small proxy that wraps XCP-ng hosts' plain connections in TLS; reports certificate verify failed when host certificates don't line up.
The ONC remote-procedure-call protocol underlying NFS.
The standard Linux logging protocol; host logs can be forwarded to a remote collector for monitoring without installing a local agent.
A virtual Ethernet device the hypervisor uses to connect a VM's NIC to a host bridge.
The user-space process that serves a VM's virtual disk under SMAPIv1; a common throughput bottleneck for backup and replication.
The reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol of the IP suite.
Intel's confidential-computing feature isolating VMs from the hypervisor (Intel's counterpart to AMD SEV-SNP).
A hardware-isolated environment for running code and data confidentially.
A minimal UDP file-transfer protocol, commonly used in PXE boot.
Allocating storage space on demand as data is written, rather than reserving the full disk size up front. Used by NFS and local-ext SRs (not LVM-based block SRs).
CPU cache of address translations; its flush behaviour matters for hypervisor performance.
Encryption layer for network connections (HTTPS, LDAPS, etc.); modern successor to SSL.
A readable configuration file format.
A hardware (or virtual) root of trust storing keys and measurements; required by Windows 11 guests.
A high-resolution CPU cycle counter; its handling is critical during VM live migration.
The connectionless, best-effort transport protocol of the IP suite.
Modern platform firmware interface replacing legacy BIOS; supports Secure Boot.
Oracle's Linux kernel build shipped with Oracle Linux.
Centralised management of desktops, mobiles, and other endpoints.
A string identifying a resource (URLs are a kind of URI).
The primary time standard; clock skew between hosts causes subtle failures.
A security appliance combining firewall, IPS, filtering, and more.
A 128-bit identifier; XAPI keys VMs, hosts, and SRs by UUID.
Converting/moving a VM from one hypervisor to another (e.g. VMware to XCP-ng).
VMware APIs that offload storage operations to the array; needs a vendor host-side plugin.
https://docs.kernel.org/block/ublk.html
VMware's bundled private-cloud stack; a migration source for XCP-ng.
A CPU presented to a guest VM; too few vCPUs starves parallel workloads such as backup workers, and oversubscription across hosts can hurt performance.
XAPI term for a single virtual disk (what VMware calls a VMDK, and what libvirt calls a volume). VDIs live inside an SR and are attached to VMs as virtual block devices.
https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/lvm.8.html#DESCRIPTION
Legacy display standard; the basic emulated graphics adapter for VMs.
Nvidia's mechanism for slicing one physical datacentre GPU (T4, A10, L4, etc.) across multiple VMs; requires a supported card and a GRID license.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VHD_(file_format)
XAPI term for a virtual NIC attached to a VM. Each VIF is bridged to a network (which maps to a physical PIF or bond). Compare with PIF (physical equivalent).
An IP address not bound to a single physical interface, used for failover or load balancing.
A way to segment network traffic at the switch/bridge level so different groups of devices appear to be on separate networks.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_machine, also called _guest_
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMDK
Remote-framebuffer protocol used for VM consoles.
The 24-bit segment ID that isolates tenants on a VXLAN overlay.
The virtual NUMA topology presented to a guest VM so it can make NUMA-aware decisions internally.
An encrypted tunnel extending a private network across untrusted links.
A VM sold as a hosting product.
Memory dedicated to a GPU's framebuffer and workloads.
Multiple independent routing tables coexisting on one device.
VMware's hyper-converged software-defined storage.
Windows framework for application-consistent snapshots; used by guest-aware backups.
A software-emulated TPM chip required by Windows 11 for secure boot and disk encryption. XCP-ng 8.3 introduced vTPM support.
Overlay encapsulating Layer-2 over UDP/IP to scale tenant networks beyond VLAN limits.
A filter that inspects and blocks malicious HTTP traffic to web apps.
A network spanning sites or regions.
An open-source security monitoring / EDR platform (agent plus server).
Microsoft's driver certification program; relevant to signing paravirtual Windows guest drivers.
https://github.com/xapi-project/xen-api
https://wiki.xenproject.org/wiki/XCP_Overview
https://xcp-ng.org/
The 9.x release line of XCP-ng (tracking newer Xen and a refreshed dom0).
The web management interface used to administer XCP-ng pools, hosts, backups, and networking.
The legacy Windows desktop client for XenServer/XCP-ng management, maintained by Citrix/Cloud Software Group.
Citrix's commercial Xen-based hypervisor; XCP-ng is the open-source platform that shares much of its lineage.
A high-performance journaling filesystem; an option for dom0/host storage.
The open-source web management interface for XCP-ng (and XenServer). Replaces XenCenter. Provides the Console tab (noVNC), backup jobs, resource scheduling, and the XAPI REST proxy.
The Node.js backend process inside XOA; its memory heap limit must be raised to actually use extra RAM given to the VM.
The version 5 (current stable) web UI of Xen Orchestra.
The next-generation Xen Orchestra UI, rolled out alongside XO5.
/management/manage-at-scale/xo-web-ui/
A lightweight XO component deployed near a pool to offload backup/replication traffic.
Hyper-convergence solution based on LINSTOR
Citrix/Cloud Software Group's XenServer 9 release line.
Official Xen Project security advisories documenting vulnerabilities and fixes.
The text-based local management console running directly on the XCP-ng host, accessible via keyboard/monitor.
XCP-ng/XenServer's VM export/import archive format.
A copy-on-write filesystem with integrity checking, snapshots, and RAID-like features.
